topicCandidates: A duty-first comparison for creative and media work across Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services, Artist, Entertainer, Journalist, Cultural Activities, Business Manager, and statuses without activity restrictions.
Searchable occupation maps for graphic design, digital product and media work, film and video production, photography, games, advertising, publishing, and independent artistic practice.
The difference between a useful search title and a residence-status conclusion: employer, contract, output, audience, commercial context, artistic independence, and principal duties remain decisive.
Portfolio, education, experience, contract, remuneration, production schedule, client, foreign-news-organization, and artistic-career evidence that may become relevant under different routes.
Mixed creative work, multiple clients, side work, self-employment, online content, and transitions between employed specialist work and operating a creative business.

routeComparisons.activityBoundary: Specialized natural-science, humanities, or foreign-culture work under a contract with a Japanese public or private organization, excluding activities assigned to listed neighboring statuses.
rolesToExamine: UI, UX, web, or digital product designer
routeComparisons.warning: The official example 'designer' supports discovery, not automatic eligibility for every design title. Duties, qualification relationship, contract, and exclusions still require review.

routeComparisons.activityBoundary: Income-producing artistic activity in music, fine arts, literature, or another artistic field, excluding activity assigned to Entertainer.
routeComparisons.warning: A creative job title does not establish an artistic career, sufficient income, or the boundary from commercial production and employed specialist work.

routeComparisons.activityBoundary: Entertainment and specified entertainment-business activity, including advertising activity, broadcast or film production, commercial photography, and commercial recording or filming.
routeComparisons.warning: The exact activity, production, contracting and inviting organizations, duration, position, remuneration, and applicable landing-criteria category matter.

routeComparisons.activityBoundary: Reporting and other journalistic activity under contract with a foreign news organization.
routeComparisons.warning: Photography, editing, or publishing for a domestic company is not converted into Journalist activity by using a press-related title.

routeComparisons.activityBoundary: Unpaid academic or artistic activity, or specialized study of Japanese culture or arts under expert guidance, subject to the route's exclusions.
rolesToExamine: unpaid creative practitioner studying under an expert
routeComparisons.warning: This route is not a substitute for paid creative employment.

routeComparisons.activityBoundary: Genuine operation or management of a business in Japan rather than merely performing freelance creative services.
routeComparisons.warning: Calling oneself a freelancer, founder, or creative director does not establish business-management activity.

userSituations: A graphic designer comparing an employed agency role, in-house product-design job, and independent client practice.
A UI or UX designer whose title mixes research, product planning, visual design, and software-adjacent duties.
A game artist, animator, motion designer, or VFX artist whose work may be employed specialist design, independent art, or part of a commercial production.
A filmmaker comparing directing, production, camera, editing, acting, advertising, and corporate-video work.
A photographer comparing fine-art practice, foreign-news photojournalism, commercial photography, studio work, and event assignments.
A content creator, YouTuber, influencer, or social-media professional whose income may come from a Japanese employer, foreign clients, advertising, sponsorship, platforms, or their own business.
A creative worker combining employment with commissions, exhibitions, royalties, or multiple clients and needing an outside-activity analysis.
A creative-agency founder who performs production work as well as genuinely operating and managing the business.
edgeCasesAndExceptions: Photographer is a particularly unsafe title-only classification: fine-art photography, foreign-news photography, and commercial photography appear in materially different route contexts.
Film worker is not one immigration category. Performance, production, corporate specialist work, journalism, and independent artistic creation require different fact patterns.
Graphic design may be employed specialized design or independent artistic work; the medium alone does not settle the route.
Digital media and content creator are umbrella labels. The actual output, client, contract, revenue, audience, and principal activity must be identified.
A creator publishing online for foreign clients from Japan still needs a status and work-authority analysis; remote delivery does not make the activity legally invisible.
Game design can mix visual art, narrative, product planning, programming, marketing, and production. The article must not present one universal route.
Art director and creative director may describe hands-on specialist work, artistic authorship, or genuine business management; seniority and the word director are not determinative.
A foreign-news contract is central to Journalist. Domestic publishing, corporate communications, and general documentary work should not be routed there from title alone.
Commercial photography is expressly named in the Entertainer materials, but the implementation must not extrapolate an unsourced universal answer for wedding, event, product, or studio work.

Side commissions, royalties, exhibitions, platform income, and multiple short contracts may raise outside-activity, notification, tax, and evidence issues even where the principal job is clearly authorized.
Statuses based on personal or family position may permit broad work, but professional licensing, tax, business, labor, and other laws still apply.

contentImpacts.reason: Give creative workers one activity-first comparison across employed design, independent art, entertainment production, foreign-news work, unpaid cultural study, business operation, and unrestricted work statuses.
Add common graphic, visual, brand, UI, UX, web, digital-product, motion, multimedia, game, advertising, and content-design language while preserving duty and qualification warnings.
Deepen the distinct artistic, production, commercial-photography, film, broadcast, and foreign-news boundaries and connect them to the comparison guide.
Make the unpaid artistic-study boundary visible without presenting Cultural Activities as a paid-work route.
Make ordinary titles discoverable even where the answer is a comparison rather than one status article.

scopeBoundaries: Do not create one residence-status article for every occupation title; occupations and statuses are not one-to-one.
Do not claim that every designer qualifies for Engineer/Specialist or every filmmaker and commercial photographer qualifies for Entertainer.
Do not turn search aliases into approval claims or job whitelists.
Do not provide unsourced universal treatment for influencers, YouTubers, wedding photographers, foreign-client remote workers, or other fact-sensitive models.
Keep copyright, model releases, location permits, drone rules, professional licensing, tax, and business compliance in later law or integration coverage except for clear cross-links.
Keep new and materially rewritten guidance at needs-review until explicit human editorial approval.
